result.note: Stage 2d lenient handler-statement mode + kotlin ?? fail-loud. The 19% of handler bodies that declined the stage-2c speculative parse were probe-isolated to four corpus idioms (cluster labels first suggested bare assignment, but a controlled probe proved assignment innocent): paren-less `if`, word operator `not`, shorthand object literals `{ a, b }`, and `;` separators. A `lenient_statements` flag on the Parser admits exactly those four forms ONLY while speculatively parsing @on_*/on_* handler bodies; the main grammar is frozen (a boundary test pins each form as still-rejected in function bodies / trait configs, so whether e.g. paren-less if becomes legal generally remains a deliberate future decision, not a side effect). MEASURED effect: handler bodies analyzed 4062/5013 (81.0%) -> 4864/5013 (97.0%); declined 951 -> 149 (3.0%). Differential over the 2303-file authority corpus: Rust pass rate 2256/2303 (97.96%), 0 regressions vs baseline -- figures byte-identical to before, so lenient mode is provably confined to handler-body analysis and changes no file's parse verdict. Also in this rebuild: map_binary_operator's catch-all previously returned unmapped operators VERBATIM (contradicting its own fail-loud doc) -- `??` emitted into invalid Kotlin; it now errs loudly (no elvis lowering is honest while ValType has no nullable variant). No wasm_bindgen export changed; 8 exports intact. cargo test 224 passed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean. Source changes are committed together with this receipt.
